related_questions.question: Is there a government debt relief program?

text_blocks.snippet: While the government doesn't offer a general debt relief program for all types of debt like credit cards, it does provide assistance and resources for specific types of debt, such as student loans and tax debt. For other types of debt, such as credit cards, individuals can explore options like debt management plans, debt settlement, or bankruptcy.
Government Programs for Specific Debt Types:

list.title: Student Loans:
list.snippet: The government offers various student loan forgiveness and repayment programs, including Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), income-driven repayment plans, and loan consolidation options.

list.title: Tax Debt:
list.snippet: The IRS has programs like Offer in Compromise (OIC) and installment agreements that can help individuals settle their tax debts for less than the full amount owed or pay it off over time.

list.title: Child Support Debt:
list.snippet: The California Child Support Debt Reduction Program (CSDRP) helps parents reduce past-due child support payments to the government.

list.title: SBA Debt Relief:
list.snippet: The U.S. Small Business Administration offers debt relief options for small businesses, particularly related to COVID-19 relief programs, according to the Small Business Administration (.gov).

list.title: Debt Management Plans (DMPs):
list.snippet: Non-profit credit counseling agencies can help individuals create a DMP to streamline monthly payments to credit card companies.

list.title: Debt Settlement:
list.snippet: Individuals or companies can negotiate with creditors to settle debts for less than the full amount owed.

list.title: Bankruptcy:
list.snippet: A legal process involving federal courts, where individuals can seek relief from debt.

list.title: Be wary of scams:
list.snippet: There are many fraudulent offers claiming to represent government debt relief programs, especially for credit card debt.

list.title: Seek professional advice:
list.snippet: Consulting with a non-profit credit counseling agency or a financial advisor can help individuals understand their options and make informed decisions.

list.title: Explore all options:
list.snippet: Researching all available resources and programs, both government and private, is crucial to finding the best solution for individual circumstances.
